title: observability: token-level KV cost/latency dashboards, tracing sampling, and alert tuning refinements
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: Token-level cost and latency breakdowns for KV-backed models are frequently requested by product teams and platform SREs to correlate user-facing latency with internal KV cache behavior and per-token GPU cost. The previous dashboards lumped KV cache activity into aggregate request counters which hid pathological cases (cold prefix storms, high miss-rate tails) and produced noisy alerts. This PR refines metrics, adds trace-sampling hooks, tightens alert thresholds, and updates dashboards/docs for on-call adoption.

Summary of changes: 
- Add token-level KV metrics (token_count, kv_hits, kv_misses, kv_miss_rate) exported with per-route tagging and sample-rate controls.
- Introduce adaptive trace sampling for requests with KV miss_rate > 10% or tail latency > 95th percentile. Traces are annotated with cache state and route/model metadata.
- Update Grafana dashboard: separate panels for token-level cost (CPU/GPU token cost estimate), KV hit/miss heatmaps, per-route latency breakdown, and combined cost+latency scatter to identify regressions.
- Alert tuning: replace single top-level high-latency alert with two tiers:
  * SLO-warning (95th latency increase OR kv_miss_rate spike) - alert to platform slack channel, low urgency
  * SLO-critical (sustained 99th latency + kv_miss_rate > 15% for 5m) - page on-call, automatic model fallback runbook invoked
- Logging: add structured log fields for kv_event_type and kv_latency_ns; sanitize PII before logging.
- Docs: observability runbook updates, dashboard links, and migration notes for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Checklist: 
- [x] Metrics instrumentation added and unit-tested
- [x] Tracing integration validated in perf-canary cluster
- [x] Dashboards reviewed by SRE/Platform (Priya)
- [x] Alert thresholds validated against 4 weeks of historical traffic
- [x] Runbook and release notes written

Rollout plan: incremental rollout to canary region (us-west-2) for 48h, enable trace sampling at 0.1% global then ramp to conditional sampling. If no regressions, rollout to all regions and flip dashboards to default in Grafana namespace.

Notes: This change touches the telemetry export path; latency impact is minimal (<0.5% p95) due to batching and non-blocking exporters. KV metric cardinality is bounded by per-route tagging and a coarse prefix bucketization implemented in the exporter to keep cardinality under control.
